Can I use the result for professional work?
Yes, for estimating and ordering with a sensible waste allowance. Legal boundary placement still belongs to survey; this measures the fence you intend to build.
Should I add extra for gates and waste?
Yes — gates interrupt runs (measure them in or out consistently) and cuts waste material. Five to ten percent overage is the common planning allowance.
A fence follows the ground, and sloping ground is longer than its map projection. On steep runs, measure the slope distance or add allowance — flat perimeters understate hill fences.
How do posts relate to length?
Posts divide the length by their spacing. The Fence Post Count Calculator turns this total into post numbers for common spacings.
Can it handle several separate runs?
Add them: a fence project is a list of runs, and the total is their sum. Keep gates and corners noted per run.
How do I allow for corners?
Corners do not change total length — the perimeter already includes them. They change the post and bracing specification, which the post calculator's notes cover.
My boundary is curved. How do I measure it?
Break the curve into short straight chords and sum them; more, shorter chords hug the curve closer. On the map, the acreage outline does this for you.
